A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LIMO, with the same title, authors, and central method. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original lighting-estimation experiments on Infinigen, Laval Indoor SV, and dynamic Blender scenes, including quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds outdoor benchmark results, field-of-view sensitivity measurements, and real-data component ablations.

M1.justification: The diffusion models, geometric conditioning maps, exposure prompts, mirror/diffuse predictions, and HDRI reconstruction procedure remain unchanged. Clarified descriptions and newly disclosed sphere-sizing information do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds a ground-truth outdoor benchmark using Laval Outdoor HDR crops (Section 4.2, Table 2, Figure 11), substantially extending quantitative single-image coverage beyond v1's indoor benchmarks. Outdoor training and qualitative outdoor examples already existed; the other datasets remain.

E2.justification: DiffusionLight and 4D Lighting remain the single-image comparators, and 4D Lighting remains the dynamic-scene comparator. The outdoor benchmark uses the same comparator set. V2's new capability matrix is research positioning, not additional empirical baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 26 randomly rotated outdoor crop sequences with three frames selected for metrics, and controlled FOV offsets from -50% to +50% on Infinigen. Existing training budgets, metrics, and original benchmark settings remain unchanged as reported.

E4.justification: V2 adds FOV-error sensitivity testing (Section 8, Figure 8) and extends component ablations to Laval Indoor SV (Section 9, Table 6). These substantially broaden analysis of geometric-input robustness and real-data component behavior, including an intensity/color tradeoff absent from v1's synthetic ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's sensitivity curves contain point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds outdoor scores, FOV-sensitivity results, and real-data ablation outcomes. For example, outdoor diffuse RMSE is 0.12 for LIMO(image), versus 0.23 for DiffusionLight and 0.25 for 4D Lighting. Retained Laval Indoor SV printed values also change: LIMO(image) glossy RMSE 0.22 to 0.21, and diffuse/glossy angular errors 2.7 to 2.6. Original video and Infinigen ablation scores remain identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, including geometric-map definitions, depth sampling, reconstruction losses, and rendering expressions, are retained. Calling the HDRI sequence a spatiotemporal volume clarifies existing mathematics; no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same claims about spatiotemporal HDR estimation, geometric grounding, and combined mirror/diffuse predictions. The introduction's five capabilities and conclusion's state-of-the-art claim retain their scope; new evidence supports existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the FOV experiment as evidence of robustness. Its real-data ablation discussion qualifies diffuse-sphere benefits: color improves while intensity accuracy worsens for some materials, hypothesized to reflect bias from predicting spheres larger than ground truth. The earlier finite-sphere and facial-cue limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Section 9 newly discloses that Laval Indoor SV predictions use spheres larger than the ground-truth probes to increase prediction resolution. This documents an implementation choice without establishing that it changed between versions. Existing hardware, training-time, data-generation, and HDRI-optimization details remain.

R1.justification: V2's Table 1 explicitly categorizes six prior methods against five capabilities, refining the existing positioning narrative. The additional bibliography entry duplicates the already cited Deep Sky Modeling paper rather than introducing a distinct work.

P1.justification: V2 tightens wording in the introduction, related work, method, and conclusion, adds acknowledgements, and inserts two supplementary analysis sections. The main section order and narrative remain substantially intact; the changes are localized editing and expansion.

P2.justification: V2 adds a capability matrix, Light Stage demonstration, FOV plot, real-data ablation table, and outdoor qualitative figure, and expands the image-results table. It also moves v1's training-example Figure 3 to supplementary Figure 7. This substantially expands and redistributes the visual material; other matched displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the existing indoor/outdoor claim with ground-truth outdoor evaluation and improves scrutiny through FOV sensitivity and real-data ablations. Reporting the diffuse component's intensity/color tradeoff makes the interpretation more informative. These are useful but bounded gains: the added outdoor benchmark is explicitly non-spatially varying, while the central dynamic-scene evidence remains unchanged.
